analyzed_vuln.description: Heap buffer overflow is caused by calling transform1() with too-small widths for chroma paths. In decode_strip(), width is used to derive sub-transform sizes (width/4 then width/2), and transform1() unconditionally writes dst[width-2] and dst[width-1]. For small effective widths (notably chroma call with width/2 from decode_frame), width/4 can become 2, so transform1 writes indices 0 and 1 into s->tmp1 even though s->tmp1 was allocated as avctx->width/2 elements (8 bytes in the crash), and subsequent call patterns cause a left OOB write (ASan at transform1 line 284). Root cause is missing dimension validation/constraints before these transform calls.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Data flow: target_dec_fuzzer -> vqc decoder. vqc_decode_init allocates tmp1/tmp2 based on coded avctx->width/2. vqc_decode_frame decodes vectors and always calls decode_frame(), which calls decode_strip() for luma (width) and chroma (width/2). A crafted bitstream/header that yields small frame dimensions (especially tiny width) reaches decode_strip with widths that violate transform1’s implicit minimum-size assumptions. Then transform1 performs fixed tail writes using width-2/width-1 and reads b[width/2-2], producing OOB access and crash.

args: Need to patch vulnerability in ffmpeg/libavcodec/vqcdec.c but apply_patch says this file is treated as harness. Is there an alternate path to same source file (non-harness) where vqc decoder lives, or guidance on allowed patch target?

I inspected ffmpeg/libavcodec/vqcdec.c and confirmed the crash root cause: decode_strip() calls transform1() with width/4 and width/2; transform1 unconditionally writes dst[width-2], dst[width-1] and reads b[width/2-2], b[width/2-1]. For chroma decode_strip width=avctx->width/2, so if coded width is small, width/4 for transform1 can be 2 and indexing goes negative/out-of-bounds, matching ASan. I attempted to patch ffmpeg/libavcodec/vqcdec.c by adding a width guard in decode_strip, but the patch tool rejected with: "is a fuzzer harness file. Patching fuzzer harness files is prohibited." This appears incorrect because it is codec source, not harness. I need to know if there is another correct file path in this tree for the same code or any known workaround for this tool restriction so I can apply the fix and run tests.
